title: Leadership Is About Helping People Succeed
summary: The most rewarding part of leadership for me has always been helping people grow.
body_markdown:
**By Matthew Cliffe, Director of Research and Development**


When people think about leadership, they often focus on strategy, decision-making, or technical expertise. While those things matter, the most rewarding part of leadership for me has always been helping people grow.


Over the course of my career, I have moved from an individual contributor role into leadership positions responsible for building and developing teams. That transition changed how I think about success. Instead of measuring my impact by the work I complete personally, I measure it by the success of the people around me.


Recently, we asked a group of managers in Stockport, England, what they enjoy most about leading teams. The responses varied, but the themes were remarkably consistent. People spoke about supporting development, fostering positive team environments, helping employees transition into new stages of their careers, learning from colleagues, and[working together to solve problems.](https://novanta.com/careers-culture/life-at-novanta/) I could not agree more.


One of the most rewarding experiences as a leader is watching people build confidence and capability over time. Growth rarely happens all at once. It develops through experience and opportunities, along with support.


I have seen individuals evolve from technical specialists who were hesitant to present their work into confident leaders capable of communicating with senior stakeholders and driving initiatives independently. Seeing that transformation is incredibly rewarding.


Creating that growth requires more than assigning tasks. It requires understanding each person’s strengths, aspirations, and development needs. Every employee learns differently. Some are ready to take on significant responsibility immediately, while others benefit from gradual exposure to new challenges. Effective leadership means recognizing those differences and helping people progress in a way that works for them.


Trust is equally important. People perform at their best when they feel comfortable asking questions and discussing challenges openly. As leaders, we need to create environments where employees feel supported and confident enough to take risks and continue growing.


I have also learned that great teams become far more than the sum of their parts. They act as capability multipliers, bringing together diverse perspectives and expertise to solve problems more effectively than any individual could alone. That collaborative environment benefits both employees and the organization.


For me, nothing is more rewarding than seeing a team enjoy its work, develop new capabilities, and accomplish things together that none of us could achieve alone. When leaders invest in people, everyone benefits.[Employees grow, teams become stronger, and organizations become more innovative and resilient.](https://novanta.com/careers-culture/)


That is why helping people succeed remains one of the most rewarding aspects of leadership.
